classification.difficultyReason: Arrange nine distinct numbers to satisfy four simultaneous equal-sum constraints.

content.prompt: Place the numbers 1 to 9 in each of the circles in the following figure so that the sums of the numbers on each straight line are equal.

spec.description: Eight blank outer circles and one blank central circle. Four straight diameters join opposite outer circles through the centre. A curved circumference joins the outer positions.
spec.mathematics: Each of the four straight lines contains three response circles. The curved circumference is not an additional equal-sum line.
spec.answerVisibility: All nine circles are blank in the question.

answer.short: One solution: centre 5; clockwise from the top: 1, 2, 3, 4, 9, 8, 7, 6. Each straight line sums to 15. Other solutions are possible.
answer.worked:
Put 5 in the centre. Pair the remaining numbers so that each opposite pair sums to 10: $(1,9)$, $(2,8)$, $(3,7)$ and $(4,6)$. Put each pair in opposite outer circles.

$$\begin{align*}1+5+9&=15\\2+5+8&=15\\3+5+7&=15\\4+5+6&=15\end{align*}$$

Every number from 1 to 9 is used once, and all four straight-line sums are equal.

spec.description: Completed nine-circle figure matching the teacher's sample arrangement.
spec.mathematics: Centre 5; clockwise from top 1, 2, 3, 4, 9, 8, 7, 6. Opposite pairs sum to 10 and each diameter sums to 15.
spec.answerVisibility: Completed numbers appear only in answer editions.
